summary: Defines a Media Gateway Control Protocol (MGCP) package for redirecting and resetting groups of endpoints, since the base protocol in RFC 3435 redirects endpoints one at a time.

eli5.summary: Instead of telling each phone line to move or restart one by one, this lets a controller say it to a whole bunch at once.

questions: how do you redirect multiple mgcp endpoints
what is the red package in mgcp
how does mgcp handle call agent failover
subtitle: Redirecting and resetting groups of endpoints in media gateways

tldr.problem: MGCP allows redirecting endpoints to a new Call Agent, but only one at a time. When a Call Agent fails over, redirecting thousands of endpoints one by one is impractical and time-consuming.
tldr.mechanism: Define an MGCP package with extensions to redirect multiple endpoints in a single command and reset groups of endpoints, plus specify backup Call Agents in a preferred order.
tldr.outcome: Media gateways can efficiently handle Call Agent failover and maintain service continuity for large trunk gateways with many endpoints.

today: RFC 3991 is an Informational document that describes an extension to MGCP deployed in products. The IETF and ITU-T have since standardized Megaco (RFC 3015) as the preferred media gateway control protocol, including standards-based security considerations. However, the RED package extensions described here remain in use in MGCP implementations for Call Agent failover scenarios.

sections.title: The Problem with One-at-a-Time Redirection
sections.content:
The base MGCP specification (RFC 3435) allows a Call Agent to redirect endpoints to a new Call Agent by setting a NotifiedEntity parameter. However, this parameter can only be set in commands that affect individual endpoints or connections. In a large media gateway (such as a trunk gateway connecting the Internet to the PSTN), there may be thousands of endpoints. If the primary Call Agent fails and a backup must take over, the new Call Agent would need to send redirect commands one endpoint at a time, which could take considerable time and consume significant bandwidth.

This document solves that problem by defining the Redirect and Reset (RED) package, which extends MGCP with three capabilities: redirecting multiple endpoints in a single command, specifying a list of backup Call Agents in priority order, and resetting multiple endpoints at once for efficient synchronization after a failure.
sections.eli5: When the main controller crashes, the backup needs to tell all the phone lines 'now you talk to me.' The old way meant sending thousands of separate messages. The new way lets it do it in a handful of messages instead.

sections.title: The RED Package Extensions
sections.content:
The RED package (version 0) defines several new parameters that can be included in MGCP commands. The first is NotifiedEntityList (encoded as RED/NL), which works like the existing NotifiedEntity parameter but allows multiple domain names to be specified as a comma-separated list. When the endpoint needs to contact a Call Agent, it tries the first domain name in the list, and if that fails (using standard MGCP retransmission), it moves on to the second domain, and so on.

The second set of extensions includes EndpointList (RED/EL) and EndpointMap (RED/MP) parameters. These allow specifying arbitrary groups of endpoints using ranges and wildcard patterns, along with a bitmap indicating which endpoints in the list should be affected by the command. This is useful for Call Agent failover situations where affected endpoints may be randomly distributed across a gateway. The third extension is the Reset parameter (RED/R), which causes specified endpoints to be reset and re-initialized to an idle state, deleting any active connections.
sections.eli5: The RED package adds three power tools. The first lets you say 'try this controller, and if it doesn't work, try that one.' The second lets you list out specific lines to affect, even if they're scattered around. The third lets you tell those lines to start fresh and forget everything.

sections.title: Endpoint Specification and Selection
sections.content:
The EndpointList and EndpointMap parameters use MGCP's existing range wildcard notation to specify endpoints. A range can specify a single endpoint, a range of endpoints (such as 1-24), or a list of ranges. The EndpointMap is a bitmap where 'T' (true) indicates the command should apply to the corresponding endpoint and 'F' (false) indicates it should not. Multiple EndpointList and EndpointMap pairs can be specified in a single command to select arbitrary combinations of endpoints.

These parameters can only be used with the EndpointConfiguration command and only when the LocalEndpointName is the gateway's virtual endpoint (such as MG@gw1.example.net). One important feature is that these parameters can be applied to out-of-service endpoints, unlike ordinary wildcard endpoint configuration. However, any configuration changes made to out-of-service endpoints will not survive a gateway restart because the provisioned values will be used instead.
sections.eli5: You write down a list of line numbers like 1-24, and then a pattern like TFTTTF that says 'apply to lines 1, 3, 4, 5 but not 2 or 6'. You can have multiple lists to cover lines scattered all over the gateway.

sections.title: Redirect and Reset Command Format
sections.content:
A redirect command using the RED package looks like this:

EPCF 1200 *@gw1.example.net MGCP 1.0
RED/N: ca1@ca1234.example.net

This tells all endpoints on the gateway (using the "all of" wildcard, *) to use ca1@ca1234.example.net as their new Call Agent. Alternatively, using the NotifiedEntityList parameter:

EPCF 1200 MG@gw1.example.net MGCP 1.0
RED/EL: *
RED/NL: ca1@myca.example.net, ca2@mybackupca.example.net

This provides a list of Call Agents to try in order. A reset command uses RED/R like this:

EPCF 1200 mg@gw1.example.net MGCP 1.0
RED/EL: ds/e1-3/[1-30]
RED/MP: TFTTTTTFFFTTTTTFFFFTFFTTFTTTFF
RED/R: reset

This selects specific endpoints from a range and resets them, which clears any active connections and returns them to an idle state.
sections.eli5: A redirect command says 'all endpoints, now use this new controller' or 'all endpoints, first try this controller, and if it's down, try this one.' A reset command says 'these specific endpoints here, start over fresh.'

sections.title: Failover and Synchronization
sections.content:
When a Call Agent fails, the backup Call Agent can use the RED package to efficiently reclaim endpoints. If the backup wants to ensure that all endpoints are in a known state, it can use the reset extension parameter to force arbitrarily distributed endpoints to idle, clearing any stale call state from the failed Call Agent. The EndpointList and EndpointMap parameters make it possible to identify and reset only the endpoints that were affected by the failure, rather than resetting the entire gateway.

The RFC includes package-specific return codes to handle error conditions. Code 800 (EndpointMap Out of Range) indicates that the EndpointMap parameters extend beyond the endpoints specified in the preceding EndpointList. Code 801 (Incorrect Usage of Parameters) indicates that EndpointList or EndpointMap were used with an endpoint name other than the gateway's virtual endpoint.
sections.eli5: When the main Call Agent crashes, the backup can say 'endpoints 1-30 with this pattern, reset.' This clears out any left-over state from the failed controller and tells those endpoints to start listening to the backup instead.
